data.title: Go Residential sues H&R REIT after shareholders reject acquisition offer
data.description:
Go Residential REIT (GO.U:CA) (GO.U) has sued H&R Real Estate Investment Trust (HR.UN:CA) (HRUFF) after the latter's investors rejected an acquisition offer by Blackstone (BX), Go, and other buyers.

The offer would have split H&R's properties among several buyers, with Go set to acquire the U.S. apartment portfolio and Blackstone and other investors, including Canada's Public Sector Pension Investment Board, getting industrial properties, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

Additionally, H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter-affiliated company CRAL would have taken over some office buildings, development sites, land, and other assets, according to the report.

The unusual arrangement reportedly sparked a revolt among major investors.

Go Residential filed proceedings against H&R and others in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, seeking a termination fee of C$102.13M and other relief arising from alleged breaches of the August arrangement agreement.

In the claim, Go Residential alleges that H&R REIT failed to comply with its contractual obligations and duty of good faith and honest performance under the arrangement agreement. The REIT allegedly failed to maintain its support for the transaction and undermined its board's prior unanimous, unqualified recommendation in favor of the transaction.

data.title: West Coast Community approves $25M share buyback program; shares surge
data.description:
• West Coast Community (WCCB) announced on Friday that its board approved a $25M share repurchase program.

  • The company may repurchase shares through open-market purchases or privately negotiated transactions, subject to market conditions.

  • The program runs through December 31, 2028, but does not require the company to buy any specific number of shares.

  • The repurchases will be funded through internal cash resources, supplemented if needed by dividends from West Coast Community Bank.

  • CEO Krista Snelling said the program reflects confidence in the company's balance sheet and long-term value while maintaining flexibility for future investments.

  • The stock surged 3% to $65.41 in the after-hours session, while the program remains subject to customary regulatory approvals or non-objections.

data.title: AstraZeneca gains additional bladder cancer indication for Imfinzi
data.description:
• The US FDA approved AstraZeneca's (AZN) Infinzi (durvalumab) in the perioperative setting in combination with Pfizer (PFE) and Astellas' (ALPMF)(ALPMY) Padcev (enfortumab vedotin) for muscle-invasive bladder cancer patients who are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy.
  • Approval was based on results from the phase 3 VOLGA trial that showed significant improvements in event-free survival and overall survival in patients on the combo vs. those on standard care.
  • The combo reduced the risk of death by 42% compared to the standard of care arm.
  • The new indication is also under review by regulators in the European Union, Japan, and several other countries.

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count slips in latest Baker Hughes survey
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. fell by 3 to 601 after rising by 1 a week ago, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. stayed flat at 463 in the week ended November 13, while gas rigs dropped 4 to 127 and rigs categorized as miscellaneous added 1 to 11.

The total rig count was up by 52, or 9.5%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 46, or 11%, from a year ago, and gas rigs were up 2, or 1.6%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin gained 2 during the past week to 275, while the Eagle Ford and the Williston Basin remained unchanged at 43 and 30, respectively.

data.title: Prairie outlines 23,000 to 25,000 BOE/d 2026 average production while holding $180M to $195M capex range
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Prairie Operating Co. (PROP) Q3 2026

Management view

  • CEO Gregory Patton said the quarter showed “the strength of our assets and the execution and excellent work our team continues to deliver across our development program,” highlighting that “average daily sales volumes increased 19% from the prior quarter to 26,117 BOE per day, and we exited the quarter at 30,229 BOE per day.”
  • Patton pointed to development execution and well performance, stating, “we have completed a large portion of our 2026 capital plan, bringing 37 wells across 5 pads online to date,” and adding that the “last 3 new pads coming online in the third quarter, all above type curve.”
  • On the Burnett pad, Patton said the program “represents an important milestone in demonstrating the value of Prairie’s acreage,” and described results including “an average maximum initial production rate of approximately 722 BOE per day per well with an 81% oil cut” and that the early data “materially derisked and validate the quality and future development potential of our acreage.”
  • CFO Michael Shelly framed the quarter’s operating leverage, saying, “Prairie generated $65.3 million of adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter, an increase of 92% from the prior quarter as sales volumes increased and unit operating costs declined,” while noting GAAP results: “Net loss attributable to Prairie was $48.9 million for the quarter.”
  • Patton emphasized operating cost actions, including that “lease operating expense declined to $5.71 per BOE from $6.85 per BOE in the prior quarter,” and added, “during the quarter, we established Stagecoach Logistics LLC to bring field maintenance, logistics and operational support functions in-house.”

Outlook

  • Management reiterated full-year operating targets through the same annualized-average framework discussed previously, with Patton stating, “ultimately, we feel very supportive of our guidance at 23,000 to 25,000 BOEs per day on the annualized average.”
  • On capital spending, Patton said, “we still feel strongly about our guidance range that was previously given of the $180 million to $195 million,” while also cautioning, “there are some inflationary expenses… we are seeing some higher costs in and around those products.”
  • On 2027, Patton said, “at this point in time, we’re not issuing ’27 guidance,” while adding, “the team has a robust amount of permits in hand.”

Financial results

  • Shelly reported, “Third quarter revenue totaled $129.5 million, up 31% from the prior quarter, including $114 million of oil revenue,” and added, “for the first 9 months, revenue reached $311.8 million.”
  • Shelly detailed profitability and key non-cash items, stating, “net loss attributable to common stockholders was $34 million or $0.26 per basic share and $0.28 per diluted share,” and that results included “$105.7 million of unrealized derivative losses.”
  • Liquidity and leverage were described as tight at quarter-end, with Shelly saying, “at September 30, we had $7.8 million of cash and $3 million available under our reserve-based credit facility,” alongside “$475 million with $472 million outstanding.”
  • Hedging and preferred-stock actions remained central, with Shelly noting, “our commodity swaps extend into 2029,” and adding, “we continue to pursue opportunities to refinance the remaining Series F preferred stock.”

Q&A

  • Leo Mariani, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC: asked about Q4 capex pacing versus the full-year budget; CEO Patton responded, “the CapEx for the year is actually at about $165 million in terms of our D&C CapEx for the year,” and reiterated, “we still feel strongly about our guidance range that was previously given of the $180 million to $195 million.”
  • Mariani, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC: asked about inflation’s impact on 2-mile well costs; Patton answered, “we’re seeing $300,000 to $500,000 of additional costs,” and cautioned, “it’s a little bit of an unknown.”
  • Mariani, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC: pressed on whether October’s ~32,000 BOE/d pace would hold; Patton said, “production has held very strong, but there’s obviously some natural decline as well,” adding, “I would not tell you that we would be exiting the year at 32,000 barrels a day.”
  • Mariani, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC: raised near-term liquidity; CFO Shelly replied, “our liquidity position will continue to improve fairly dramatically as we get into the end of Q4.”
  • Mariani, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC: asked about extending the Series F warrant deadline again; Patton said, “we are in discussions with High Trail,” and added, “we believe that an outcome will be available to us.”
  • Charles Meade, Johnson Rice & Company: asked how Burnett compared to internal expectations and offsets; Patton answered, “internally, they have beat our internal type of results,” and said peers nearby were “seeing and exhibiting equal and/or better results than we are.”
  • Meade, Johnson Rice & Company: asked about additional 2026 turn-in-lines; Patton said, “the drilling results and DUCs… would be very limited at this point in time,” and added, “most of the activity from this point forward would be benefiting Q1.”
  • Jeffrey Robertson, Water Tower Research: asked about early-2027 development cadence; Patton answered, “we’re not issuing ’27 guidance,” and added, “the quantum and number of wells… we’re not disclosing that yet.”
  • Robertson, Water Tower Research: asked how free cash flow would be used between working capital and RBL paydown; Shelly said, “we’ll continue to pay our payables,” and “we’ll continue to pay down our RBL as well as available.”
  • Robertson, Water Tower Research: asked about RBL redetermination timing and covenants; Shelly said, “we have quarterly redeterminations… I expect some perspective on that… in December,” and added, “those production metrics are… been met to date and will continue to be met.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, concentrating on liquidity tightness, capital discipline, production decline math, and preferred/warrant overhang, including Mariani’s framing that liquidity “looks a little bit tight.”
  • Management’s tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more measured in Q&A, pairing confidence with caveats, including Patton’s “we feel very supportive of our guidance” alongside “natural decline is a thing,” and Shelly’s emphasis that liquidity “will continue to improve fairly dramatically.”
  • Versus Q2, management leaned less on governance/organizational change language and more on pad performance and cost execution; analyst questioning remained anchored on production trajectory and the Series F process, now also emphasizing quarter-end liquidity levels.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q3 messaging shifted from Q2’s “transformative period” and board/management transition to operational validation, with Patton emphasizing Burnett “materially derisked” acreage and expanded proved undeveloped inventory.
  • Guidance language was largely consistent, with Q3 reiterating Q2’s updated 2026 average production band (23,000–25,000 BOE/d) and capex range ($185M–$195M in Q2; Patton reiterated $180M–$195M as the previously given range in Q3).
  • Analyst focus broadened from Q2’s initial questions on whether Burnett had started flowing to Q3’s detailed interrogation of decline pacing, year-end exit-rate uncertainty, and near-term funding flexibility.

Risks and concerns

  • Cost inflation risk was flagged by Patton: “we’re seeing $300,000 to $500,000 of additional costs… and that could continue to go up depending on the geopolitical environment,” with mitigation implied through prior-year procurement: “we had a lot of our products locked in for the year.”
  • Liquidity and leverage sensitivity was explicit in Shelly’s quarter-end figures and heavy RBL usage; management’s mitigation was improved Q4 cash generation as Shelly said liquidity “will continue to improve fairly dramatically.”
  • Capital structure overhang remained active, with Shelly stating, “we continue to pursue opportunities to refinance the remaining Series F preferred stock,” and Patton adding, “we are in discussions with High Trail.”

Final takeaway

Management characterized Q3 as a step-change quarter driven by higher volumes, lower LOE per BOE, and operational validation at Burnett that “materially derisked” Prairie’s acreage and expanded proved undeveloped inventory. Leadership reiterated support for the 2026 annual-average production range of 23,000–25,000 BOE/d and maintained capex guidance while acknowledging late-year cost inflation pressure. In Q&A, analysts concentrated on liquidity tightness, expected decline from October’s peak rate, and the timing and outcome of Series F preferred/warrant negotiations; management repeatedly pointed to improving Q4 liquidity, no near-term need for incremental development to meet RBL production metrics, and ongoing discussions with High Trail.

data.title: Cohere announces acquisition of cubic, aimed at boosting AI cyber defense
data.description:
• Canadian technology firm Cohere, which is backed by Nvidia (NVDA), announced on Friday that it has acquired AI code review platform cubic, becoming Cohere's fourth acquisition this year.
  • Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
  • "Led by founder and CEO Paul Sanglé-Ferrière, the team brings expertise across AI, security, developer tools, distributed systems, and enterprise software," Cohere wrote of cubic. "They will establish Cohere's secure coding vertical, helping accelerate the integration of enterprise-grade coding capabilities into our platform while meeting the security, governance, and deployment requirements our customers demand. Their work strengthens our ability to help organizations build, maintain, and secure software using AI within their own environments and under their own control."

data.title: Micromem prices a private placement offering of its shares
data.description:
• Micromem Technologies (MRM) annnounced on Friday a non-brokered private placement offering of its shares at a price of C$0.025 per unit for a total of up to C$250,000, subject to a 50% discretionary increase. 
  • Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant exercisable at C$0.05 per share for a period of three years. 
  • Micromem intends to use the proceeds raised through the private placement for working capital purposes and debt settlement.
